title: on_ac_power reports AC power on battery when the battery isn't named
description:
on_ac_power reports AC power on battery when the battery isn't named
BAT<n>, e.g. macsmc-battery on Apple T2 Macs (LP: #2172719).

This counts every power supply of type Battery as a battery, instead
of only those named BAT<n>, but still skips batteries of peripherals
like mice (scope Device). systemd-ac-power also goes by type and scope,
not name:
https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/main/src/shared/battery-util.c

Testing: I ran on_ac_power against fake sysfs trees (script attached to
the bug). Exit codes before / after:

  macsmc-ac offline + macsmc-battery            0 / 1  (the bug)
  LP #1980991: Type-C sink offline, no battery  0 / 0
  same + hidpp_battery_0 (scope Device)         0 / 0
  other cases (AC/BAT0, plugged in)             unchanged

On the MacBook itself, unplugged: 0 before, 1 after.

Debian 1.39 has no name check, so nothing to forward; the check is only
in the Ubuntu delta and in its proposed forward, salsa !4.
diff:
diff --git a/debian/changelog b/debian/changelog
index 362c71e..287da28 100644
--- a/debian/changelog
+++ b/debian/changelog
@@ -1,3 +1,9 @@
+powermgmt-base (1.39ubuntu2) tenacious; urgency=medium
+
+  * on_ac_power: detect batteries not named BAT<n> (LP: #2172719)
+
+ -- Johan Walles <johan.walles@gmail.com>  Sun, 01 Nov 2026 16:36:37 +0100
+
 powermgmt-base (1.39ubuntu1) stonking; urgency=medium
 
   * Merge with Debian unstable (LP: #2161446). Remaining changes:
diff --git a/on_ac_power b/on_ac_power
index 88db2df..c03f79b 100755
--- a/on_ac_power
+++ b/on_ac_power
@@ -57,8 +57,9 @@ if [ -d /sys/class/power_supply/ ]; then
     for FN in /sys/class/power_supply/*; do
 	if test -d "${FN}" && test -r "${FN}/type"; then
 	    type="$(cat "${FN}/type")"
-	    # check if the device has a battery
-	    if echo "$FN" | grep -qE '/BAT[0-9]+$' && [ "$type" = "Battery" ]; then
+	    # check if the device has a battery, not counting peripherals
+	    if [ "$type" = "Battery" ] &&
+	       [ "$(cat "${FN}/scope" 2>/dev/null)" != "Device" ]; then
 		HAS_BATTERY=yes
 	    fi
 	    # check if it's a typec and it's power role if it is.
